key_insight: Adapting only the Transformer layers most sensitive to the target task can improve fine-tuning gains while reducing degradation of general abilities.
engineering_relevance: LS-LoRA offers a simple, forward-only way to place LoRA adapters more efficiently, making PEFT more practical for math and code workloads where capability retention matters.
method: Measure layer sensitivity with input-output cosine similarity as a cheap proxy for empirical Fisher.
Insert trainable LoRA adapters only into layers with low input-output similarity.
Use this layer-selective placement to balance target-task adaptation and general-capability preservation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experiments on mathematical reasoning and code generation, where LS-LoRA improves average target-task performance and preserves more commonsense reasoning than standard all-layer LoRA.
watch_item: Layer ranking depends on the chosen proxy and task/model setting, so sensitivity estimates may need validation before deployment on new architectures or domains.
paper_title: Where to Adapt Matters: Layer-Selective Fine-Tuning for Capability Retention
